candidates.name: Opposite-endpoint return map with self-supplied Kuratowski contraction -> aligned chords
paper_items: I15 contraction estimate chi(gH)<=(1-M/U)^2 chi(H) (eq:contraction, main.tex:269-291)
candidates.statement: At an attained maximal defect D_t(x0,y)=M>0, define g on directions v at ty: x(v)=ty+p v in S_X, f(x)=tb+s w, opposite contact f(z)=tb-u w, g(v)=(ty-z)/r. On E={s-p=M} extremality forces r=u+M, so ||g(v)-g(v')|| <= (up/rs)||v-v'|| + scalar terms with up/rs=(1-M/r)(1-M/s)<=(1-M/(1+t))^2<1; binning p,u gives chi(gH)<=gamma chi(H); Darbo on the invariant closed convex C (C2) yields a fixed direction = aligned chords x=ty+pv, z=ty-rv, f(x)=tb+sw, f(z)=tb-uw, s-p=r-u=M.

final.justification: The only item with no neighbour found in any field. The eureka content is that a hypothetical positive defect M manufactures the contraction margin (1-M/r)(1-M/s) that a Darbo argument needs, removing all compactness/finite-dimension assumptions that every prior approach relied on. Downgrade risks: (i) every component is classical (Darbo, radial contact, two triangle inequalities) and once the aligned-chord target is posed the fixed-point move may be one step away (arm A of P-C1); (ii) full texts of Tingley 1987 and Kadets-Martin 2012 could not be read, so a fixed-point/return argument there is not excluded; (iii) the device may be a one-off (downstream test). Not transfer: Darbo itself is N0 transfer; the candidate is the problem-specific map and its self-supplied contraction. UPDATE 2026-10-12 (full-text re-check): downgrade risk (ii) is now largely discharged: Kadets-Martin 2012, Peralta's survey, Mori, Mori-Ozawa, Cueto-Avellaneda-Peralta, Banakh, Banakh-Cabello Sanchez, Cabello Sanchez, Fakhoury, Huang-Zhu x2, Nakamura-Tanaka and Ma 2026 were read/grepped in full; none contains a fixed-point-theorem or return-map argument. Tingley 1987 and Ding 2009 remain unread (not on arXiv) but no description attributes such a device to them. Confidence 0.45 -> 0.50; grade unchanged (N3 provisional) because test 4 and the expert query are still open. verified_checks.source: Kadets, Martin, 'Extension of isometries between unit spheres of finite-dimensional polyhedral Banach spaces', JMAA 396 (2012)
verified_checks.what_was_read: full text (10 pp., all sections incl. references)
verified_checks.finding: Method is differentiability of f and of the homogeneous extension F at smooth/non-smooth points (tangent-direction map F_y, support-functional map G_y), then Tingley's Mankiewicz-on-facet-cones step [Tingley 1987, p.377] plus Gateaux differentiability at vertices. A chord-direction map x -> (x-y)/||x-y|| appears (Lemma 3.2) only as a locally bi-Lipschitz chart for a measure-zero argument. No fixed-point theorem, no self-map of directions, no contraction, no measure of noncompactness, no invariance of domain. Finite-dimensional throughout (uses norming constants C>0 from dim<inf).
verbatim_quotes: The idea of the proof is to study the differentiability properties of f and of its homogeneous extension F.
It is shown in [7, p. 377] (using Mankiewicz result [5]), that for every cone Cj generated by an (m - 1)-dimensional face of SX there is a linear operator Aj
g(x) = (x-y)/||x-y|| ... g is injective, g(Dy) is relatively open, and g, as well as g^-1 are locally Lipschitz.
verified_checks.effect_on_grade: removes the Kadets-Martin branch of C1 downgrade risk (ii); none (confirms test-1 verdict for C1)
